mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in monthly payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 1.3 million signals labor market strength, prompting equity investors to anticipate sustained growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns within the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain negative despite the payroll employment surge, or the effect persists for less than 5 days in >70% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both GDP (GDPC1) and industrial production (INDPRO) by over 5% in the same month indicates robust demand and supply-side expansion, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and INDPRO both increase by >5% in the same month
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns do not exceed the baseline by 2% or more, or the correlation between the proxy changes and returns falls below 0.3 in a 3-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained upward trend in quarterly GDP (GDPC1) indicates growing economic activity, which compresses discount rates and boosts equity valuations, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain negative despite rising GDP, or the GDP growth rate decelerates below 2% in the subsequent quarter.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%), investors anticipate higher interest rates, reducing the present value of future cash flows and generating negative S&P 500 forward returns within the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns do not turn negative despite FEDFUNDS exceeding 4.0%, or the effect persists for less than 5 days in >50% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in retail sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) by over 2% in the same month signals robust demand across sectors, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and HOUST both increase by >2% in the same month
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns fail to exceed baseline by 1.5% or the proxies' correlation with returns drops below 0.25 in a 4-month window.

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate (UNRATE) falling below 8.0% signals a strengthening labor market, fostering investor confidence and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain negative despite UNRATE dropping below 8.0%, or the effect wanes within 30 days in >60% of triggered instances.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production (INDPRO) entering a post-recession rebound phase (vintage value < 90) indicates supply-side recovery, prompting equity investors to anticipate growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns within the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns do not turn positive despite INDPRO entering the rebound phase, or the effect lasts less than 5 days in >80% of instances.
